# 1 Enoch Chapter 84 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 84 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 84:6 — 'King of kings, God of gods, Lord of lords'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "King-of-kings, and-God-of-gods, and-Lord-of-lords" | Literal construct chains; echoes Deut 10:17 |
| LOGOS | "King of kings, and God of gods, and Lord of lords" | Same; echoes Deut 10:17 and Dan 2:47 |
| PNEUMA | "the King of kings, God of gods, Lord of lords" | Adds article before 'King' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering without the article. The Ge'ez lacks the article; the tripartite formula is a liturgical formula. The absence of the article gives the formula its iconic quality (cf. the same title without article in Rev 19:16: "King of kings and Lord of lords").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 84:7 — 'Nay' vs. 'No' for the defiant word

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "'Nay'" | Archaic; preserves solemnity of the refusal |
| LOGOS | "'Nay'" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "'No'" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'Nay' (EMET/LOGOS). The archaic form suits the liturgical register of this prayer. The idea is that no created being can utter a negation against God's will — the archaic 'Nay' preserves the solemnity better than 'No.'

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Register preserved.

---

## 84:1 — Scope of Enoch's pastoral address

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-pray-and-implore-thee and-request-thee to-do-righteousness" | Three verbs: pray, implore, request |
| LOGOS | "I pray and implore you and request of you to do righteousness" | Same three verbs |
| PNEUMA | "I plead with you, I beg you" | Two verbs; slightly more urgent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS three-verb formula. The Ge'ez has three distinct verbs of entreaty, and this should be preserved. The accumulation of verbs intensifies the appeal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
